newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen flat after giving up earlier gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen flat after giving up earlier gains.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE ended Wednesday's day session flat as Japanese government bond futures gave up earlier gains, traders said.
The June Euroyen contract rose to 99.28 in the morning, following a jump in the key December JGB futures contract.
"Euroyen futures at the moment are following JGB futures' moves," a trader at a Japanese city bank said.
The December JGB futures contract ended 0.10 higher at 124.00, but was well off its all-time high of 124.36 touched in the morning session.
Traders cited Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita's remarks as partly responsible for triggering profit-taking in the JGB market in the afternoon.
Matsushita said the mechanism for an autonomous recovery by Japan's economy was now in place.
"As JGB and Euroyen futures have reached a very high level, the market was sensitive to such remarks," said the city bank trader.
The Nikkei stock index's rebound from its intraday low today also helped to cool down the bullish mood in the JGB and Euroyen futures markets, traders said.
Turnover of the June Euroyen futures contract was 81,131 contracts.
In the interbank call market, the key unsecured overnight rate was at 0.49 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.

Although the Bank of Japan maintained a neutral stance in this morning's money market operation, players are inclined to concentrate their fund raising on shorter-dated instruments, which is keeping the overnight rate firm, traders said.
About 90 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.52 percent, and about 10 billion yen worth of two-month CDs at 0.50 percent.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.49 percent.
All rates were unchanged from Tuesday. -- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
